Verified (a) non-Ofsted jurisdictions receive an EMPTY override string (byte-identical prompt regression for england/wales/scotland/NI, incl. NI residential+domiciliary variants + '' + None), (b) Ofsted school/early_years/childrens_home each get the correct SECTOR OVERRIDE block with pupil/child language and the 'pastoral'/'caseload' lifts, (c) migration m022 applied — need_review_signals table + RLS enabled+forced + policy `need_review_signals_rls` + lookup index all present, (d) process_need_review_signals against real DB: threshold=3 correctly stays silent on hits 1+2, injects a Need Reviewer risk on hit 3 with correct shape (id starts 'needreview_', severity 'high', text 'Need Reviewer — insufficient visit time raised 3 times for Edith...', suggested_resolutions populated) while preserving existing risks, (e) case-insensitive name matching works (Edith/edith/EDITH counted together), (f) full Ofsted no-op verified — for jurisdictions 'ofsted'/'ofsted_school'/'ofsted_early_years': zero risk injection AND zero DB rows written, (g) within-meeting dedupe collapses same person+category to 1 row, (h) invalid categories, empty names, and non-dict entries are dropped, (i) independent person+category tuples accumulate independently, (j) all 7 CONCERN_CATEGORIES + THRESHOLD=3 constant match the spec, (k) ANALYSIS_SYSTEM_PROMPT contains the need_review_signals JSON schema + category enum, and the other 3 prompts (DOC_EVIDENCE / SUMMARY_ONLY / PII_SCAN) do NOT accidentally reference need_review_signals. Also source-verified wiring: transcription_pipeline.py:384-385 and review.py:1358-1360 both call process_need_review_signals with the CORRECT effective_jurisdiction (ofsted_/northern_ireland_ suffixed variant, not the plain jurisdiction), and both are inside database.with_admin() (bypassing RLS for the write, safe because WHERE clauses explicitly filter by org_id). Frontend loads cleanly on the preview URL.
critical_code_review_comments: utils/need_reviewer.py::process_need_review_signals — the per-signal COUNT query fires ONCE PER SIGNAL inside a for-loop, and if multiple signals for the same person+category somehow slipped past the dedupe (they can't in current code, but if a future refactor changed dedupe), you'd double-count the same row. Not a bug today, but consider a single SQL after all inserts. Very low priority.

utils/need_reviewer.py — the injected risk `id` is `needreview_<lowercased_name>_<category>`. If two DIFFERENT people share a first name (e.g. 'Edith Jones' and 'Edith Smith' both reach threshold), their risks would share the same id and the rescan merge in review.py line 1411 (existing_risk_ids set) would silently drop the second one. Real-world edge case worth a follow-up hashing of the full name.

utils/ai.py — Ofsted override lifts the 'pastoral' ban and the 'caseload → people we support' rule, but the base ANALYSIS prompt likely has other adult-social-care-specific language rules (e.g. dignity/best-interests/DoLS) that will still fire for schools. Not verified in this pass since no real Ofsted transcript was run through the LLM here (see below). Recommend a spot-check by main agent with a school transcript.

transcription_pipeline.py:384 and review.py:1359 — the `from utils.need_reviewer import process_need_review_signals` is inlined inside the function body rather than at module top. Works, but adds ~microsecond import overhead per meeting and hides the dependency from static analysis. Move to top of file.

review.py::_run_rescan_background — Need Reviewer risks are merged into existing risks by id (line 1410-1412). If a rescan happens AFTER 3 hits already accumulated, then during rescan a 4th need_review_signal for the same person+category would insert ANOTHER row into need_review_signals (bringing count to 4), and re-inject a needreview_ risk with 'raised 4 times…' text. The merge would dedupe by id (same id), so the OLD '3 times' text would be kept and the fresh '4 times' text dropped. Consider: fresh takes precedence on id collision, OR dedupe before insert. Low priority — cosmetic staleness.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 135 did NOT run a real end-to-end 3-meeting audio-upload → transcription → AI-analysis → DB → UI test. Rationale: (1) that path burns significant OpenAI credits and requires a browser mic or a paste-transcript endpoint (this app has neither — only /api/processing/{id}/upload accepts a real audio blob and immediately enqueues a job); (2) the main agent already unit-tested `process_need_review_signals` in isolation and got the correct behaviour on hits 1/2/3 and the Ofsted no-op; (3) this iteration extends that with a REAL Postgres round-trip (22 tests, all green) — every code path in need_reviewer.py is exercised against a live DB including RLS-relevant inserts. The only remaining unverified glue is the two call-sites in transcription_pipeline.py:384 and review.py:1359, both source-reviewed and correct (effective_jurisdiction pattern matches, admin-conn used, INSERT ordering places the risk mutation BEFORE the analyses INSERT so the injected risk lands in the persisted risks column). If a future iteration wants to close that last gap, the cheapest path is to seed a meeting row directly + call transcription_pipeline._process_meeting with a stubbed transcript that already contains 'insufficient time with Edith'-style repetition and monkeypatch _analyze_meeting to return a canned dict — no real OpenAI call needed. Standards-seeded orgs available: admin@supervision.com (england/CQC), alex@1two.one (scotland), hello@1two.one (ofsted school). MFA bypass procedure in /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
